variables.name: Total water storage
variables.definition: All the water stored on and under the land (lakes, rivers, soil moisture, groundwater, snow and ice), weighed from space by how much it pulls on two satellites. Shown as the difference from the long-term average.
variables.source: GRACE / GRACE-FO satellites (NASA, DLR, GFZ); GFZ GravIS Level-3 grid
caveats: No data between GRACE and GRACE-FO (2017-07 to 2018-05) and a few other single months; gaps are left empty, not filled.
The satellites see blobs about 300 km across, so small basins and reservoirs blur into their surroundings.

variables.name: Rainfall (GPCP)
variables.definition: How much rain and snow falls, averaged over each month, from a blend of satellite and rain-gauge measurements.
variables.source: GPCP v2.3 monthly precipitation (NASA GSFC / GEWEX, served by NOAA PSL)
caveats: GPCP reads too dry after 2019 in several regions (we checked it against MERRA-2 and against Lake Kariba's satellite water level). The default window stops at 2019 for that reason.
variables.warning: GPCP drifts dry after 2019. Trends that include 2020 onwards can show a drying that is not real.

variables.name: Rainfall (MERRA-2 model)
variables.definition: Monthly rainfall from NASA's MERRA-2 reanalysis: a weather model that is constantly corrected with observations.
caveats: At a few places MERRA-2 rainfall has artificial jumps (for example Colombia in 2008 and 2021, Vietnam from 2016-17). Compare with GPCP before trusting a trend.
Sampled at a few points inside the region, not a full area average.

variables.name: Root-zone soil wetness
variables.definition: How wet the soil is down to about 1 metre, where plant roots drink: 0% is bone dry, 100% is fully soaked.
caveats: NASA POWER soil wetness has a step change from October 2026, so the series stops at September 2026.
Model output, sampled at a few points inside the region.

variables.name: Surface soil wetness
variables.definition: How wet the top 5 cm of soil is: 0% is bone dry, 100% is fully soaked. It reacts within days to rain and heat.
caveats: NASA POWER soil wetness has a step change from October 2026, so the series stops at September 2026.
Model output, sampled at a few points inside the region.

variables.name: Air temperature
variables.definition: The average air temperature 2 metres above the ground, the height of a weather station.
caveats: The series stops at September 2026 because of a step change in NASA POWER land fields from October 2026.
Model output, sampled at a few points inside the region.

variables.name: Lake water level
variables.definition: The height of the reservoir's surface, measured by radar satellites that pass overhead every 10 days.
variables.source: G-REALM satellite radar altimetry (USDA FAS / NASA; TOPEX/Poseidon, Jason-1/2/3, Sentinel-6)
caveats: Reservoir levels are set by people as well as by climate: dam releases and allocation rules move them.
Monthly means of 10-day passes; months without a pass are left empty.

variables.name: Hydropower generation
variables.definition: Electricity produced by the grid's hydropower plants each month. This is the consequence: what the water does to the lights.
caveats: New dams raise output over time, so a rising trend can mean more dams, not more water.
Monthly records start in 2010-2019 depending on the country, so many are short.

variables.name: El Niño index (ONI)
variables.definition: How much warmer (El Niño, positive) or cooler (La Niña, negative) than normal the central Pacific Ocean is. It shifts rain around the world.
variables.source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center Oceanic Niño Index (not NASA)
caveats: The same global series for every region: it is context, not a measurement of the region.
Already an anomaly (no seasonal cycle), and a 3-month running mean, so neighbouring months are strongly linked.

methods.deseasonalize: Subtract each calendar month's mean over the chosen window (as pipeline.trends does).
methods.sen_slope: Median of all pairwise slopes on the real time axis (gaps do not compress time).
methods.mann_kendall: Two-sided Mann-Kendall S with tie correction; Hamed-Rao (1998) variance correction for autocorrelation using significant rank-autocorrelation lags of the Sen-detrended series; Yue-Wang fallback if the corrected variance is not positive (as pipeline.trends).
methods.ci: 95% confidence interval on Sen's slope by the Gilbert (1987) rank method, using the (corrected) variance of S.

validation.what: GRACE TWS, window 2002-04..2026-08, seasonal cycle removed, Hamed-Rao on. 'browser_*' is pipeline.explorer.browser_stats (a line-by-line copy of web/src/components/explore/stats.ts) run on the rounded values in explorer/r/*.json; 'trends_*' is trends.json (pymannkendall Hamed-Rao, Sen's slope on the real time axis). Small differences come from rounding the published values to 0.01 cm (more ties) and from trends.json rounding p to 5 decimals.

notes: GravIS has two solutions dated in the same calendar month for 2011-10, 2015-04; they are averaged.
35 of 293 months have no GRACE/GRACE-FO solution (including the 2017-07..2018-05 mission gap); they are left missing, not interpolated.
